tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

1	# Kitty: shared trip costs — design
2	
3	## Intent
4	
5	A small command-line tool for tracking shared costs on trips with friends, so
6	that at the end everyone knows who owes whom. The owner is not a programmer;
7	their friend Sam will drive it from scripts and a spreadsheet, so every report
8	prints machine-readable JSON and expenses export to CSV.
9	
10	## Goals
11	
12	- Record expenses (with flexible splits and foreign currencies) and repayments.
13	- Show balances, a settle-up plan, per-person history, a category report, and
14	  a CSV export.
15	- Money is always exact: no floating point, shares always sum exactly to the
16	  expense total.
17	- Clear error messages and exit status 1 on any bad input — never a traceback.
18	
19	## Non-goals
20	
21	- No GUI, no network, no live exchange rates, no multi-file/multi-trip
22	  management (one `kitty.json` per folder).
23	- No editing of expenses (remove and re-add instead), no removing payments.
24	
25	## Anti-goals
26	
27	- Old expenses changing value when a rate is later changed.
28	- Silently rounding bad input (e.g. `12.345`) instead of refusing it.
29	- Silently losing history (e.g. by removing a member who appears in records).
30	
31	## Constraints
32	
33	- Runs with the macOS system Python (**3.9.6**) and the standard library only.
34	  No `match`, no `X | Y` type syntax at runtime, no third-party packages.
35	- Invoked as `python3 -m kitty <command> ...` from the folder containing the
36	  `kitty/` package. Data lives in `kitty.json` in the **current working
37	  directory**.
38	
39	## Approaches considered
40	
41	1. **Small package with separate modules + stdlib `unittest` tests** — chosen.
42	   Money math, storage, commands, and CLI parsing each in their own module;
43	   easy for Sam to read and extend; tests pin down the cent-distribution rules.
44	2. **Single `kitty.py` file** — same invocation, fewer files, but everything
45	   tangled; harder to extend. Rejected.
46	3. **Store raw inputs only, recompute everything each run** — conflicts with
47	   rate locking (old expenses would be re-valued). Rejected; each expense
48	   stores its rate, converted amount, and computed shares at creation time.
49	
50	The owner left the build approach to the builder; option 1 is the builder's
51	call.
52	
53	## Decided behaviour (by the owner)
54	
55	### Commands
56	
57	- `init CUR` — create a new kitty with base currency `CUR`.
58	- `member add NAME`, `member remove NAME`, `member list`.
59	- `expense add PAYER AMOUNT DESCRIPTION...` — prints the new expense's ID.
60	  Options: `--among A,B` | `--exact A=30,B=20` | `--shares A=2,B=1` |
61	  `--percent A=60,B=40` (at most one of these), `--currency CUR`,
62	  `--date YYYY-MM-DD` (default today), `--category NAME` (default `other`).
63	- `expense list`, `expense remove ID`.
64	- `payment add FROM TO AMOUNT` with `--currency`, `--date`.
65	- `rate set CUR VALUE` — 1 CUR = VALUE base currency.
66	- `balances`, `settle`, `history NAME`, `report`, `export FILE`.
67	
68	### Output formats (JSON, money as strings with two decimals)
69	
70	- `member list`: `["Alice", "Bob"]`
71	- `expense list`: `[{"id": 1, "date": "2026-07-14", "payer": "Alice",
72	  "description": "Dinner", "amount": "45.00", "currency": "USD",
73	  "base_amount": "41.40", "category": "food",
74	  "shares": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}]`
75	- `balances`: `{"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "-20.70"}`
76	- `settle`: `[{"from": "Bob", "to": "Alice", "amount": "20.70"}]`
77	- `history Bob`: `[{"date": "2026-07-14", "description": "Dinner",
78	  "change": "-20.70", "balance": "-20.70"}]`
79	- `report`: `{"food": {"Alice": "20.70", "Bob": "20.70"}}`
80	- Money is in the base currency, except an expense's own `amount`.
81	- `export FILE`: CSV with columns `id, date, payer, description, amount,
82	  currency, category, base_amount`.
83	
84	### Errors
85	
86	Any invalid input (unknown member, non-number amount, etc.) prints a message
87	saying what is wrong and exits with status 1. No tracebacks.
88	
89	### Amounts
90	
91	- Must be a positive number with at most two decimals. `12.345`, `0`, `-5`,
92	  `abc` are all **refused**, never rounded.
93	
94	### Currencies and rates
95	
96	- `rate set` for the base currency is refused.
97	- An expense/payment in a non-base currency with no rate set is refused, with
98	  a message saying no rate is set and how to set one.
99	- The rate in effect when an entry is added is **locked** into that entry:
100	  its `base_amount` is computed and stored then. Changing the rate later only
101	  affects new entries.
102	- Conversion: `base_amount = amount × rate`, rounded to the cent, **halves
103	  up** (0.125 → 0.13).
104	
105	### Splitting
106	
107	- Default: equally among everyone who is a member **at the time the expense
108	  is added**.
109	- Every share is first its exact amount **rounded down** to the cent; the
110	  leftover cents are then handed out **one each, in order**: the order typed
111	  in `--among`/`--shares`/`--percent`/`--exact`, or the order people joined
112	  the group when split among everyone.
113	  - €10 among Alice, Bob, Cara → 3.34, 3.33, 3.33.
114	  - 10.00 with `--shares A=1,B=2` → A 3.34, B 6.66.
115	- `--exact` amounts are in the expense's own currency and must add up exactly
116	  to the expense amount; `--percent` values must add up to 100. Otherwise
117	  refused.
118	- Shares are stored in the base currency and always add up exactly to
119	  `base_amount`.
120	
121	### Settling
122	
123	While anyone is not even: the person who owes the most pays the person who is
124	owed the most, the smaller of the two amounts (evening out at least one of
125	them). Ties are broken alphabetically, ignoring case. Payments are listed in
126	the order they are produced.
127	
128	### Names
129	
130	- Case-insensitive: `alice` and `Alice` are the same person. Adding `alice`
131	  when `Alice` exists is refused. Any spelling works in any command.
132	- Always displayed as first added.
133	- Names may not contain `,` or `=`.
134	
135	### Removing members
136	
137	Refused if the person appears in any expense or payment (as payer, sharer,
138	sender or receiver). Otherwise allowed.
139	
140	## Builder's calls (owner agreed to these as proposals or left them open)
141	
142	- **Foreign-currency splits:** convert the total first (halves up), then split
143	  `base_amount` with the round-down-and-hand-out rule. For `--exact` in a
144	  foreign currency, the weights are the exact amounts, so each base share is
145	  `base_amount × exact_i / amount` rounded down, leftovers in listed order.
146	  (In the base currency this reproduces the exact amounts.)
147	- **One splitting algorithm:** every split is "weights → exact proportional
148	  part of the base total in cents → floor → leftover cents one each in list
149	  order". Equal = weight 1 each; shares = the given numbers; percent = the
150	  given percentages; exact = the given amounts. Leftover is always fewer
151	  cents than there are people.
152	- **Weights validation:** `--shares` and `--percent` values must be positive
153	  numbers (decimals allowed). `--exact` values follow the amount rules
154	  (positive, ≤ 2 decimals). Names in any list must be members, may not repeat,
155	  and the list may not be empty. Only one of the four split options at a time.
156	- Rates must be positive numbers; any number of decimals allowed; stored as a
157	  string. Setting a rate again replaces it.
158	- Payment to oneself is refused. Payer of an expense need not be among the
159	  sharers.
160	- Expense IDs start at 1, increase, and are never reused after removal.
161	- `balances` lists all current members in join order, including `0.00`.
162	  `balance = paid base_amounts − own shares + payments sent − payments
163	  received`. (Paying someone back raises your balance and lowers theirs.)
164	- Ordering: `expense list`, `history`, and `export` sort by date, then by
165	  the order entries were typed. Expenses and payments share one internal
166	  sequence counter so they interleave correctly in `history`.

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.
